All committers have signed the CLA.

Warnings
:warning: The Pull Request doesn't contain any release info, if your changes are relevant for external developers please add an entry to the release info file, including the consequences of the change and how it affects external developers. For detailed infos please refer to the [release documentation guide](https://github.com/shopware/shopware/blob/trunk/delivery-process/documenting-a-release.md).

Tested against a real production catalog (local copy, 6.7.14.1, ~22k products, 8,988 exported rows, Google Shopping CSV whose body template still had a `{% set %}` ternary on `product.cover`).

Associations from `ProductExportGenerator::getAssociations()`: the patch removes exactly the two bogus paths (`cover.product.cover.media`, `mainCategories.product.mainCategories.category`); all other associations unchanged. The new bare tokens (`url`, `brand`, ...) resolve to `null` in `EntityDefinitionQueryHelper::getAssociationPath()` and are dropped by `array_filter`.

`product-export:generate --force` (`read_buffer_size: 50`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| runtime | 215 s / 231 s (2 runs) | 61 s |
| peak RSS | 3.35 / 3.26 GB | 1.28 GB |
| output | | byte-identical (`cmp`) |

Single-path `{% set %}` and `{% for %}` aliasing unchanged.
Not covered: the partial-generation (queue) path; #19564 is unrelated and still open. 👍

Nice catch, and the fix does what it says! I tried it on a local shop with product export and SEO URL templates, including the three shipped export templates: the output stays the same, the recursive associations are gone, and an export preview with the cover ternary went from 1.6 s to 0.3 s.

One case changes, @pcbeingused333: a fallback between two objects followed by a nested relation, for example `{% set media = product.cover.media ?? product.manufacturer.media %}{{ media.mediaFolder.name }}`. On trunk it renders (more by luck), with this change the alias is dropped, `mediaFolder` is not loaded and the template fails with "Impossible to access an attribute on a null variable". Could the variable keep all its paths, so later uses resolve against each of them? If not, a short release note would help.

Thanks for trying it, @mkucmus, and for the concrete case. The alias is no longer dropped: a `{% set %}` whose value resolves to several paths now keeps all of them, and later accesses are resolved against each one. `{% set media = product.cover.media ?? product.manufacturer.media %}{{ media.mediaFolder.name }}` now yields both `product.cover.media.mediaFolder.name` and `product.manufacturer.media.mediaFolder.name`, so `mediaFolder` is loaded again, and the bogus glued path from the original issue stays gone. Added unit tests for the fallback case and for a `{% for %}` over such a value (`media.thumbnails`), which previously glued the paths together.

(Disclosure: this change was prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude) and submitted by a human contributor.)
